name: Shamator Town
description: Headquarters of Shamator district, the 16th and one of the newest districts of Nagaland formed in 2022 from parts of Tuensang and Kiphire, known as the Brotherhood District and home to Yimkhiung and Tikhir Naga tribes.
facts: Lies in Shamator district, Nagaland at about 1800 m elevation
Created as district HQ on 4 March 2022
Base for exploring Zungki River and surrounding Yimkhiung villages
Sources: Wikipedia, shamator.nic.in

name: Zungki River
description: Largest tributary of the Tizu River flowing through Shamator district, offering scenic gorges, blue waters, sandy banks in dry season, and opportunities for picnics, angling and photography in a remote hilly setting.
facts: Official tourist place listed on shamator.nic.in as natural/scenic beauty
Originates near Changdong forest and flows south through Noklak, Shamator and Kiphire before joining Tizu
Part of the proposed Tizu-Zungki National Waterway (NW-101)
Coordinates approximate for the Shamator section; Sources: official NIC, Wikipedia

name: Yakor Village
description: Yimkhiung Naga village about 12 km from Shamator town, offering authentic tribal culture, traditional houses, agricultural fields and scenic ridge views in the eastern hills.
facts: Lies in Shamator district, Nagaland; population about 1078 (2011)
Known for traditional Yimkhiung lifestyle and crafts
Accessible as a cultural day visit from Shamator HQ
Sources: Wikipedia, Census 2011, OSM

name: Sangphur Village
description: One of the larger villages in Shamator circle with a population over 2300, featuring traditional Naga settlement patterns, community life and proximity to the district headquarters for cultural immersion.
facts: Lies in Shamator district, Nagaland; population 2314 (2011)
About 10 km from Shamator HQ
Part of the official recognized villages list
Sources: Census, shamator.nic.in, postal data

name: Chessore
description: Sub-divisional headquarters and village cluster in Shamator district, serving as an administrative and cultural center for the Chessore area with surrounding villages and local festivals.
facts: Lies in Shamator district, Nagaland; Chessore Sub-Division
Host to local sports meets and community events
Part of Shamator-Chessore assembly constituency
Sources: official NIC village lists, OSM, local reports

name: Shamator Village
description: Historic village adjacent to the district headquarters, inhabited primarily by Yimkhiung Nagas, offering insights into traditional architecture, community life and the area's tribal heritage.
facts: Lies in Shamator district, Nagaland; population about 1159 (2011)
Recognized village listed on official district site
Close to HQ for easy cultural visits
Coordinates approximate; Sources: Census, shamator.nic.in

name: Metümnyo Festival Grounds
description: Venue for the traditional five-day harvest festival of the Yimkhiung tribe held in August after millet harvest, featuring communal rituals, dances, youth engagements and prayers for the departed.
facts: Celebrated in the second week of August in Shamator district
Includes cleaning rituals, path repairs and soul prayers
Official festival listed on shamator.nic.in
Best experienced during festival period; Sources: official NIC

name: Zungki River Valley Picnic Spot
description: Wide valley basin along the Zungki River near Shamator offering flat sandy areas for family picnics, shallow pools and views of surrounding forested hills in a peaceful remote setting.
facts: Popular local day-trip destination in Shamator district
Features sandy banks and forest surroundings
Accessible from Shamator town via river crossings
Coordinates approximate; Sources: local tourism descriptions, official river page

name: Kohima Town
description: Capital of Nagaland and headquarters of Kohima district, a hilly town at about 1444 m elevation known for its role in World War II and as the base for exploring Angami Naga culture and nearby valleys.
facts: Lies in Kohima district, Nagaland at approximately 1444 m elevation
Site of the decisive 1944 Battle of Kohima
Base for Hornbill Festival and visits to Kisama and Dzukou
Sources: Wikipedia, kohima.nic.in

name: Kohima War Cemetery
description: Commonwealth War Graves Commission cemetery on Garrison Hill in central Kohima, commemorating 1420 Allied soldiers who died in the 1944 Battle of Kohima, with the famous epitaph 'When you go home tell them of us and say for your tomorrow we gave our today'.
facts: Lies in Kohima district, Nagaland; maintained by CWGC
Contains 1420 Commonwealth burials and memorial to 917 cremated
Located on the site of the 1944 Battle of Kohima tennis court
Open daily; Sources: Wikipedia, CWGC, kohima.nic.in

name: Kisama Heritage Village
description: Open-air Naga Heritage Village 12 km south of Kohima between Kigwema and Phesama, designed as a traditional Naga village with morungs of all ethnic groups and the permanent venue of the annual Hornbill Festival.
facts: Lies in Kohima district, Nagaland; 12 km from Kohima on NH
Name amalgamates Kigwema and Phesama
Venue for Hornbill Festival (typically 1-10 December)
Sources: Wikipedia, kohima.nic.in

name: Khonoma Green Village
description: Western Angami Naga village 20 km west of Kohima, India's first green village (declared 2005) with terraced fields, community conservation, and the Khonoma Nature Conservation and Tragopan Sanctuary protecting Blyth's Tragopan.
facts: Lies in Kohima district, Nagaland; elevation about 1621 m
Declared India's first Green Village in 2005
Features Khonoma Nature Conservation and Tragopan Sanctuary
Sources: Wikipedia, kohima.nic.in

name: Dzukou Valley
description: High-altitude alpine valley at about 2438-2452 m on the Kohima (Nagaland)-Senapati (Manipur) border, known as the Valley of Flowers of the Northeast for its rolling meadows, dwarf bamboo, wildflowers and streams.
facts: Lies primarily in Kohima district, Nagaland (border with Manipur)
Elevation 2438-2452 m; approached via Viswema or Jakhama
Popular moderate trek from Kohima side
Sources: Wikipedia, kohima.nic.in; border note

name: Japfu Peak
description: Second highest peak in Nagaland at 3048 m in the Barail Range, about 15 km south of Kohima, home to the world's tallest rhododendron tree and offering panoramic views over Dzukou Valley and surrounding hills.
facts: Lies in Kohima district, Nagaland; elevation 3048 m
Holds Guinness record for tallest rhododendron tree (~20 m)
Trek starts from Kigwema village
Sources: Wikipedia, official tourism

name: Nagaland State Museum
description: State museum on Bayavü Hill in Kohima displaying ethnographic collections of Naga tribal artefacts, traditional dresses, ornaments, weapons and models of village life, operated by the Department of Art and Culture.
facts: Lies in Kohima district, Nagaland on Bayavü Hill
Opened to public on 25 November 1970
Showcases artefacts from all Naga tribes
Sources: Wikipedia, artandculture.nagaland.gov.in

name: Mary Help of Christians Cathedral
description: Catholic cathedral in Kohima noted for architecture blending traditional Naga house elements, with a 16-foot carved wooden crucifix among Asia's largest, consecrated in 1991 and serving the Diocese of Kohima.
facts: Lies in Kohima district, Nagaland
Consecrated January 1991; capacity about 4500
Architecture incorporates Naga house facade elements
Sources: Wikipedia, kohimadiocese.org

name: Dzüleke Village
description: Angami Naga eco-village near Kohima known for community conservation, terraced fields and as a quieter base for nature walks and birdwatching in the western hills.
facts: Lies in Kohima district, Nagaland
Community-managed conservation area
Accessible as a day or overnight visit from Kohima
Sources: tourism guides, local reports
